```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Setup"
library(opal)
library(ggplot2)

data(io_yft_data)
data(io_yft_parameters)
data(io_yft_map)
data(io_yft_reference)

ref   <- io_yft_reference
d     <- io_yft_data
n_ts  <- d$n_year
truth <- ref$truth$trajectory
ss3   <- ref$ss3$trajectory
sf    <- ref$ss3$sizefreq

# Model outputs precomputed by data-raw/generate-io-yft-vignette-cache.R, so
# the article renders without rebuilding the RTMB model
cache <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "io_yft_vignette_cache.rds", package = "opal"))
opal_m <- cache$models$age_sf

fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
options(knitr.kable.NA = "—")
fleet_name <- function(f) sprintf("%d: %s", as.integer(f), ref$fleet_names[as.integer(f)])
last <- function(df, v) df[[v]][df$ts == max(df$ts)]

series_col <- c("Simulated truth" = "#D4AC0D", "SS3" = "grey20", "opal AGE-SF" = "#C2185B")
scale_series <- list(scale_colour_manual(values = series_col, name = NULL, drop = TRUE))
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
```

This article compares three views of one simulated Indian Ocean yellowfin
tuna stock: the **simulated truth** from the spatial operating model that
generated the data, the **Stock Synthesis 3 (SS3)** assessment of those data
developed by the IATTC analyst team, and **opal AGE-SF**, an opal model of
the same data configured to match that SS3 model as closely as opal can
while every estimated parameter stays identified.
How far opal AGE-SF is from SS3 measures how well opal reproduces an
established assessment; how far either is from the truth measures how well
a single-region assessment recovers a spatially structured stock. The
differences between opal and SS3 that remain after matching their settings
are described in @tbl-differences and @tbl-estimation.

Both the simulated data and the SS3 model come from the Spatial Stock
Assessment Simulation Experiment, an international, blinded experiment in
which analyst teams assessed data simulated from spatially explicit
operating models without knowing the truth
([Goethel et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1111/faf.12819)). The IATTC
team's SS3 model was one of the assessments submitted to it.

```{r}
#| label: data-size
n_catch <- sum(d$catch_obs_ysf > 0)
n_cpue  <- nrow(d$cpue_data)
n_lf    <- length(d$lf_year)
n_sf    <- length(unique(sf$data$ts))
n_comp_cells <- n_lf * d$n_len + n_sf * length(sf$bins)
```

The data are not a toy example. The model runs `r n_ts` quarterly time
steps (1952–2015) for 16 extraction fisheries. It is conditioned on
`r fmt(n_catch, 0)` non-zero fishery-quarter catches and fits
`r n_cpue` longline CPUE observations in four quarterly series,
`r fmt(n_lf, 0)` length compositions over `r d$n_len` bins of 5 cm and
`r n_sf` index size compositions over `r length(sf$bins)` bins: about
`r fmt(n_comp_cells, 0)` composition cells in all. opal AGE-SF estimates
`r opal_m$fit$n_par` parameters, most of them the `r n_ts` quarterly
recruitment deviations. This is comparable to the operational IOTC
yellowfin assessment the operating model was conditioned on
([Fu et al. 2018](https://iotc.org/sites/default/files/documents/2018/10/IOTC-2018-WPTT20-33.pdf)),
which is also a quarterly, multi-fleet, age-structured Stock Synthesis
model fitted to catch, CPUE and length compositions over a similar period.

Everything needed is bundled with the package: the data, SS3's and the
operating model's results, and the stored opal fit.

# The three models

## The simulated truth

The data are replicate 4 of the Indian Ocean yellowfin operating model (OM)
of the
[Spatial Stock Assessment Simulation Experiment](https://aaronmberger-nwfsc.github.io/Spatial-Assessment-Modeling-Workshop/articles/OM_description_YFT.html).
The OM was built in the Spatial Population Model software (SPM; Dunn,
Rasmussen and Mormede 2015) and conditioned on Indian Ocean Tuna Commission
(IOTC) fishery data
([Dunn, Hoyle and Datta 2020](https://iotc.org/sites/default/files/documents/2020/10/IOTC-2020-WPTT22AS-19_Rev1.pdf)).
The experiment and its results across all participating assessments are
described by [Goethel et al. (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1111/faf.12819). The
OM is spatially explicit:

* **Space and time.** The population lives on a 5° × 5° grid of 159 ocean
  cells, in quarterly time steps from 1952 to 2015 (256 quarters), with ages
  1–28 quarters (28 is a plus group).
* **Recruitment.** One stock with one Beverton–Holt stock–recruitment
  relationship (steepness 0.8) on the total spawning biomass. Quarterly
  recruitment strength varies (lognormal, SD 0.6), and each quarter's
  recruits are spread across cells by a spatial apportionment layer with its
  own random variation.
* **Movement.** Fish move between cells every quarter according to habitat
  preferences for sea surface temperature, chlorophyll-a and distance,
  separately for immature and mature fish. Maturation moves fish from the
  immature to the mature state.
* **Fishing.** Seven gear-type fisheries remove their observed catches
  exactly, cell by cell, using exploitation rates.
* **Data.** Catch (without error), longline CPUE, length frequencies and tag
  recaptures are simulated cell by cell.

For the experiment, the simulated data were aggregated to the four regions
of the IOTC yellowfin assessment and to a single area. Because the data are
simulated, the true spawning biomass and unfished spawning biomass (B0) are
known. The truth files report them by assessment region; here they are
summed over the whole domain. Spawning biomass is mature biomass at the
start of the quarter, before fishing, in tonnes, the same definition as
SS3's and opal's.

## The SS3 model

The SS3 model (SS3 v`r ref$ss3$version`) is the IATTC analyst team's
single-region estimation model for the experiment, built by Mark N.
Maunder, Haikun Xu and Carolina Minte-Vera. It treats each quarter as a
model "year", so it runs `r n_ts` time steps. It keeps the four-region
structure in its fleets: its 16 extraction fisheries are gear × region
combinations (for example, `fishing_ll_1` to `fishing_ll_4` are longline in
regions 1–4). Its mean length-at-age is the OM's own
([Fu et al. 2018](https://iotc.org/sites/default/files/documents/2018/10/IOTC-2018-WPTT20-33.pdf),
after Fonteneau and Gascuel 2008), so growth is known exactly. Selectivity is
age-based, and the longline survey has both a CPUE index and generalised
size compositions.

## opal AGE-SF

The bundled opal inputs were produced from SS3's data, control, parameter
and report files by an SS3-to-opal converter
([wcpfc-bet-single-region](`r ref$source$repository`), `code/rtmb`). They
reconcile exactly with SS3 for catch, the index, the length compositions
and biology (M, weight, maturity and spawning potential at age). opal takes
the same time steps (`n_year = ` `r n_ts`, `n_season = 1`) and SS3's ages
1–`r d$n_age`, so the opal age index equals the SS3 age.

```{r}
#| label: dimensions
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("Time steps (quarters)", "Ages", "Extraction fisheries",
               "Index series (longline CPUE, one per quarter)",
               "Fisheries with length compositions", "Length bins",
               "Index size-composition bins"),
  value = c(n_ts, d$n_age, 16, 4, length(d$lf_fishery_f), d$n_len, length(sf$bins))),
  col.names = c("Quantity", "Value"))
```

The bundled inputs (`io_yft_data`, `io_yft_parameters`, `io_yft_map`) use
opal's default length-based selectivity. AGE-SF changes them in two ways,
shown in [Building AGE-SF](#building-age-sf): it uses SS3's age-based
selectivity curves, and it fits SS3's index size compositions with SS3's
weight. Other differences between SS3 and opal stay, as structural choices
rather than settings to match.

## How the three differ

The population and fishing processes:

| | Simulated truth (SPM) | SS3 | opal AGE-SF |
|---|---|---|---|
| Space | 159 cells, movement between them | One region; fleets keep the four regions | As SS3 |
| Recruitment | Beverton–Holt (h = 0.8) on total SSB; spatially apportioned | Beverton–Holt; deviations sum to zero; age-0 recruits at *t* | SS3's steepness and σ_R; unconstrained deviations; age-1 recruits at *t* + 1 |
| Growth | The OM's | `GrowthModel 3`, age-specific K (the OM's growth) | The same, through `get_growth()` with `log_k_mult` |
| Fishing | Seven gear fisheries; exploitation rates by cell | 16 fisheries; hybrid F (Baranov), F and M act together through the quarter | 16 fisheries; the quarter's catch is removed at the start, then M acts |

: Structural differences between the simulated truth, SS3 and opal AGE-SF in the population and fishing processes. {#tbl-differences}

The estimation choices, which only the two assessments have:

| | SS3 | opal AGE-SF |
|---|---|---|
| Selectivity | Age-based double normal (fisheries), logistic (survey); mirrors | The same curve families and mirrors, on age (`sel_basis_f = 2`) |
| Selectivity bounds | Per parameter (index inflection 8–18 quarters) | ±20 on opal's age scale for every `par_sel` |
| Timing of observations | Index and compositions at mid-quarter | Everything at the start of the quarter |
| Index | One series, one analytic catchability | Four quarterly series, four estimated catchabilities |
| Index size compositions | 14 bins from 30 cm, λ = 0.51 | The same bins and λ |
| Priors | None (λ = 0 on parameter priors) | opal's defaults: N(0, 2) on `par_sel`, weak normal priors on log B0 and log q |
| Equilibrium plus group | Iterated to 3 × the number of ages | Closed-form geometric tail (≈5e-5 difference in SPR0) |

: Differences in estimation choices between SS3 and opal AGE-SF. {#tbl-estimation}

Catch timing is the largest difference. At SS3's own parameter values, it
alone moves opal's spawning biomass by up to 10%, because under heavy catch
opal ends each quarter with more fish than the Baranov equation leaves. The
priors are kept on purpose (see [How we got here](#how-we-got-here)).

# Building AGE-SF

## Growth

The bundled inputs already use SS3's age-specific K growth. (The first
conversion used opal's single-k Schnute curve, which was 5–16 cm too long
at ages 4–8 and moved the fitted stock size well away from SS3's; opal now
implements `GrowthModel 3` through `get_growth()`.)

```{r}
#| label: growth
p <- io_yft_parameters
laa_opal <- get_growth(d$n_age, d$A1, d$A2, exp(p$log_L1), exp(p$log_L2), p$log_k,
                       min_age = d$min_age, log_k_mult = p$log_k_mult,
                       k_mult_ages = d$k_mult_ages,
                       plus_group_adjust = isTRUE(d$growth_plus_group_adjust))
```

opal's mean length-at-age differs from SS3's by at most
`r fmt(max(abs(laa_opal - ref$ss3$length_at_age$length)), 4)` cm.

## Age-based selectivity

SS3 uses double normal curves (`age_selex` pattern 20) for the fisheries,
mirrors (pattern 15) for fisheries 15 and 16, and a logistic curve
(pattern 12) for the longline index. `sel_basis_f = 2` evaluates opal's
curves directly on age, and `convert_ss3_selex_to_rtmb(basis = "age")`
converts SS3's estimated parameters, held in `io_yft_reference`, to opal's
`par_sel` scale:

```{r}
#| label: age-selectivity
sp  <- ref$ss3$sel_par
pat <- ref$ss3$sel_pattern

# SS3 fleet whose parameters each opal fishery uses: fisheries 1-16 are SS3
# fleets 1-16 (15 and 16 mirror 14 through pattern 15), and the four
# quarterly index series 17-20 are SS3's survey, fleet 17.
ss3_fleet <- c(seq_len(16), rep(17L, 4))
mirror <- pat$pattern[ss3_fleet] == 15L
ss3_fleet[mirror] <- pat$special[ss3_fleet[mirror]]
ss3_pars <- t(vapply(ss3_fleet, function(fl) {
  v <- sp$value[sp$fleet == fl]
  c(v, rep(0, 6 - length(v)))
}, numeric(6)))

d_age <- io_yft_data
d_age$sel_basis_f <- rep(2L, d_age$n_fishery)
p_age <- io_yft_parameters
p_age$par_sel <- convert_ss3_selex_to_rtmb(ss3_pars, d_age$sel_type_f,
                                           sel_lengths = d_age$len_mid,
                                           basis = "age", sel_ages = d_age$age_a)
```

SS3's final selectivity is −999 for every double normal, meaning "no
adjustment": the descending limb is the plain normal curve.
`convert_ss3_selex_to_rtmb()` turns −999 into −9, which pulls the whole limb
down. Setting the final selectivity to the unadjusted curve's own value at
the oldest age reproduces "no adjustment" exactly at the starting values
(the final selectivity is fixed, so this is an approximation once the peak
or descending width move):

```{r}
#| label: no-adjustment
# Unadjusted descending limb at the oldest age, as in sel_double_normal()
dn_unadjusted_end <- function(par, x) {
  n <- length(x)
  bin_width <- x[2] - x[1]
  peak <- mean(x) + par[1] * sd(x)
  peak2 <- peak + bin_width + (0.99 * x[n] - peak - bin_width) / (1 + exp(-par[2]))
  exp(-(x[n] - peak2)^2 / (exp(par[4]) * sd(x)^2))
}
for (f in which(d_age$sel_type_f == 2L & ss3_pars[, 6] <= -999)) {
  p_age$par_sel[f, 6] <- max(qlogis(dn_unadjusted_end(p_age$par_sel[f, ], d_age$age_a)), -20)
}
```

The map estimates every selectivity parameter SS3 estimated (phase > 0),
with SS3's mirrors. On the age scale, SS3's plateau and ascending-width
parameters for several fisheries are near −10 to −15, outside opal's default
`par_sel` bounds of ±7, so the bounds are widened to SS3's ±20:

```{r}
#| label: map-bounds
est <- matrix(NA_integer_, d_age$n_fishery, 6)
k <- 0L
for (fl in unique(ss3_fleet)) {
  cols <- sp$par[sp$fleet == fl & sp$phase > 0]
  ids <- k + seq_along(cols)
  k <- k + length(cols)
  for (f in which(ss3_fleet == fl)) est[f, cols] <- ids
}
map_age <- io_yft_map
map_age$par_sel <- factor(as.vector(est))

age_bounds <- function(parameters, map, lim = 20) {
  active <- unlist(lapply(names(parameters), function(n)
    rep(n, if (is.null(map[[n]])) length(parameters[[n]]) else nlevels(droplevels(map[[n]])))))
  b <- get_bounds(list(par = setNames(numeric(length(active)), active)), parameters)
  b$lower[b$parameter == "par_sel"] <- -lim
  b$upper[b$parameter == "par_sel"] <- lim
  b
}
```

At SS3's parameters, opal's age-based curves reproduce SS3's
selectivity-at-age:

```{r}
#| label: sel-check
sel0 <- get_selectivity(d_age, p_age$par_sel, pla = NULL, len_mid = d_age$len_mid,
                        age_a = d_age$age_a)[, 1, ]
s0 <- data.frame(fishery = rep(seq_len(nrow(sel0)), times = ncol(sel0)),
                 age = rep(d_age$age_a, each = nrow(sel0)), sel = as.vector(sel0))
cmp <- merge(s0, ref$ss3$sel_age, by = c("fishery", "age"), suffixes = c("_opal", "_ss3"))
```

The largest difference over all fisheries and ages is
`r fmt(max(abs(cmp$sel_opal - cmp$sel_ss3)), 4)`; `r nlevels(map_age$par_sel)`
selectivity parameters are estimated.

## Index size compositions

SS3's generalised size compositions for the survey use `r length(sf$bins)`
bins with lower edges `r paste(sf$bins, collapse = ", ")` cm, in numbers,
with `r length(unique(sf$data$ts))` observations and sample sizes of
`r min(sf$data$nsamp)`–`r max(sf$data$nsamp)`. SS3 puts the population
below 30 cm into the first bin, and the last bin is open-ended; opal's
default `"accumulate"` tails do both. `prep_lf_data()` takes the 5 cm
length compositions and the size compositions as two wide tables, each on
its own bins; only opal's predictions are rebinned. In opal the index is
four quarterly series, so each observation goes to the index fishery of its
quarter; the four share one selectivity curve, as SS3's survey does. SS3's
lambda of 0.51 on the size compositions becomes an `lf` lambda on those four
fisheries.

```{r}
#| label: sizefreq-data
# The bundled 5 cm compositions as a wide table of counts. lf_n carries
# SS3's variance adjustment (n / lf_var_adjust), so it is undone here for
# prep_lf_data() to reapply.
lf_wide <- function(d) {
  n_raw <- d$lf_n * d$lf_var_adjust[d$lf_fishery]
  counts <- d$lf_obs_in * n_raw
  colnames(counts) <- as.character(d$len_lower)
  data.frame(fishery = d$lf_fishery, year = d$lf_year, month = 1L, ts = d$lf_year,
             counts, check.names = FALSE)
}
# SS3's size compositions as a wide table of counts (proportion x sample size)
sizefreq_wide <- function(ref) {
  sf <- ref$ss3$sizefreq$data
  wide <- stats::reshape(sf[, c("ts", "fishery", "nsamp", "bin", "obs")],
                         idvar = c("ts", "fishery", "nsamp"), timevar = "bin",
                         direction = "wide")
  counts <- as.matrix(wide[, paste0("obs.", ref$ss3$sizefreq$bins)]) * wide$nsamp
  colnames(counts) <- as.character(ref$ss3$sizefreq$bins)
  data.frame(fishery = wide$fishery, year = wide$ts, month = 1L, ts = wide$ts,
             counts, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}

# Both bin schemes end at the top of the model's length grid
top <- d_age$len_bin_start + d_age$n_len * d_age$len_bin_width
d_sf <- prep_lf_data(
  d_age,
  list(lf_wide(d_age), sizefreq_wide(ref)),
  lf_switch     = d_age$lf_switch,
  lf_minbin     = d_age$lf_minbin,
  lf_maxbin     = d_age$lf_maxbin,
  lf_var_adjust = d_age$lf_var_adjust,
  lf_addtocomp  = d_age$lf_addtocomp,
  lf_upper_edge = c(top, top))

index_f <- sort(unique(d_age$cpue_data$fishery))
lf_lambda <- rep(1, d_sf$n_fishery)
lf_lambda[index_f] <- sf$lambda
d_sf$lambdas <- list(lf = lf_lambda)
```

```{r}
#| label: inputs-check
#| include: false
# The inputs built above must be the stored fit's: compare a numeric
# fingerprint with the one data-raw/generate-io-yft-vignette-cache.R stored.
fingerprint <- function(data, parameters, map) {
  rapply(list(data = data, parameters = parameters, map = lapply(map, as.integer)),
         function(v) c(length(v), sum(as.numeric(v), na.rm = TRUE)),
         classes = c("numeric", "integer", "logical"), how = "unlist")
}
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(fingerprint(d_sf, p_age, map_age), cache$inputs_fingerprint)))
```

At SS3's solution (before fitting), opal's predicted size compositions are
close to SS3's expected values:

```{r}
#| label: sizefreq-check
ss3_like <- function(o, e, n) { i <- o > 0; -sum(n[i] * o[i] * log(e[i] / o[i])) }
sf_pred <- function(nm) merge(sf$data, cache$models[[nm]]$sizefreq,
                              by = c("fishery", "ts", "bin"))
chk <- sf_pred("age_sf_start")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("Largest difference in a proportion", "Mean absolute difference",
               "SS3-style multinomial likelihood, SS3's expected values",
               "The same, opal's predictions", "SS3's reported likelihood (Report.sso)"),
  value = c(fmt(max(abs(chk$predicted - chk$expected)), 4),
            fmt(mean(abs(chk$predicted - chk$expected)), 4),
            fmt(ss3_like(chk$obs, chk$expected, chk$nsamp), 1),
            fmt(ss3_like(chk$obs, chk$predicted, chk$nsamp), 1), "1,067.4")),
  col.names = c("At SS3's solution", "Value"))
```

The remaining difference is the timing: SS3 takes the survey at
mid-quarter, opal at the start. (The SS3-style likelihood is
−Σ N o log(e / o); opal's multinomial differs by a constant.)

# Fit

AGE-SF is fitted in two steps: first without the size compositions (AGE),
from SS3's solution, then with them, from AGE's estimates. Fitting takes
several minutes, so the article uses the stored fit, made from exactly
these inputs. `data-raw/generate-io-yft-fits.R` also polishes the optimum
with Newton steps and runs `opal_check()` with a gradient tolerance of 1e-4.

```{r}
#| label: fit
#| eval: false
control <- list(eval.max = 10000, iter.max = 10000)
age <- opal_fit(opal_obj(d_age, p_age, map_age, bounds = age_bounds(p_age, map_age),
                         control = control), n_passes = 2L)
p_start <- opal_rtmb(age)$env$parList(age$fit$opt$par)
age_sf <- opal_fit(opal_obj(d_sf, p_start, map_age, bounds = age_bounds(p_start, map_age),
                            control = control), n_passes = 2L)

# The stored fit
age_sf <- opal_read(system.file("extdata", "io_yft_age_sf_fit.rds", package = "opal"))
summary(age_sf)
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-table
v <- opal_m$fit
w <- opal_m$nll_w
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("Estimated parameters", "Objective", "Index", "Length compositions",
               "Index size compositions (× 0.51)", "Recruitment", "Priors",
               "Max |gradient|", "opal_check()"),
  value = c(v$n_par, fmt(v$objective, 2), fmt(w[["index"]], 1), fmt(w[["length"]], 1),
            fmt(w[["sizefreq"]], 1), fmt(w[["recruitment"]], 1), fmt(w[["prior"]], 1),
            formatC(v$max_gradient, format = "e", digits = 1),
            if (isTRUE(v$passes)) "passed" else "failed")),
  col.names = c("AGE-SF", "Value"))
```

# How we got here

AGE-SF is the last of a sequence of opal fits, each making one change from
the one before. `SS3-SEL` holds selectivity at SS3's estimates;
`LEN` is the bundled inputs (`io_yft_map`), with opal's length-based
selectivity estimated; `AGE-SF-NP` is SS3's configuration exactly, with the
priors switched off as well.

```{r}
#| label: bridge
br <- cache$bridge
h <- ref$history[2, ]
bridge <- rbind(
  data.frame(model = "SS3-SEL", change = "SS3's selectivity held fixed",
             sel_free = 0L, B0 = h$B0, dep = h$terminal_depletion, check = NA),
  data.frame(model = br$model, change = br$change, sel_free = br$sel_free, B0 = br$B0,
             dep = br$terminal_depletion,
             check = ifelse(br$passes, "passed",
                            ifelse(br$positive_hessian, "failed", "failed (Hessian)"))),
  data.frame(model = "SS3", change = NA, sel_free = NA, B0 = ref$ss3$ssb0,
             dep = last(ss3, "static_dep"), check = NA),
  data.frame(model = "Simulated truth", change = NA, sel_free = NA, B0 = ref$truth$b0,
             dep = last(truth, "static_dep"), check = NA))
bridge$B0 <- bridge$B0 / ref$ss3$ssb0
bridge$model[bridge$model == "AGE-SF"] <- "**AGE-SF**"
knitr::kable(bridge, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2, 3, 0), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Fit", "Change from the row above", "Selectivity parameters",
                           "B0 / SS3 B0", "Terminal SSB / B0", "opal_check()"))
b <- setNames(seq_len(nrow(br)), br$model)
```

* Held at SS3's selectivity, opal reproduces SS3's stock size closely.
  Estimating selectivity lowers it, whether the curves are opal's
  length-based ones (LEN) or SS3's own age-based ones (AGE), so the
  selectivity basis is not what separates opal from SS3.
* The index size compositions inform the index's selectivity, which
  otherwise only the CPUE trend informs. They move opal's depletion from
  `r fmt(br$terminal_depletion[b[["AGE"]]], 3)` to
  `r fmt(br$terminal_depletion[b[["AGE-SF"]]], 3)`, towards SS3's.
* Switching off the priors, as SS3 does, leaves
  `r br$sel_free[b[["AGE"]]] - br$sel_free[b[["AGE-SF-NP"]]]` selectivity
  parameters with a flat likelihood (plateau widths at a single age,
  knife-edge limbs, and the plateau and descending limb of asymptotic
  fisheries). AGE-SF-NP holds them fixed, and its Hessian is still not
  positive definite, so its standard errors cannot be used; SS3, run without
  a Hessian, does not report on this. Its stock status differs little from
  AGE-SF's. Without priors the likelihood also has more than one optimum:
  started from SS3's solution rather than AGE's estimates, AGE-SF-NP stops
  at a worse optimum with a larger stock. AGE-SF keeps opal's priors, which
  identify every parameter SS3 estimated.

# Stock status

```{r}
#| label: trajectories
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Spawning biomass (top) and static depletion SSB / B0 (bottom): the simulated truth, SS3 and opal AGE-SF."
traj <- rbind(
  data.frame(truth, series = "Simulated truth"),
  data.frame(ss3, series = "SS3"),
  data.frame(opal_m$trajectory, series = "opal AGE-SF"))
traj$series <- factor(traj$series, names(series_col))
long <- rbind(data.frame(ts = traj$ts, series = traj$series, value = traj$ssb / 1e6,
                         panel = "Spawning biomass (million t)"),
              data.frame(ts = traj$ts, series = traj$series, value = traj$static_dep,
                         panel = "SSB / B0"))
ggplot(long, aes(ts, value, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  scale_series +
  labs(x = "Time step (quarter)", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: status-table
compare <- function(x, y) {
  m <- merge(x, y, by = "ts")
  c(mean_pct = mean(abs(100 * (m$ssb.x / m$ssb.y - 1))),
    max_dep = max(abs(m$static_dep.x - m$static_dep.y)))
}
opal_tr <- opal_m$trajectory
B0 <- c(ref$truth$b0, ref$ss3$ssb0, opal_m$B0)
tab <- data.frame(
  model = names(series_col),
  B0 = B0 / 1e6,
  B0_truth = B0 / ref$truth$b0,
  terminal = c(last(truth, "static_dep"), last(ss3, "static_dep"),
               last(opal_tr, "static_dep")),
  pct_truth = c(NA, compare(ss3, truth)[["mean_pct"]], compare(opal_tr, truth)[["mean_pct"]]),
  dep_truth = c(NA, compare(ss3, truth)[["max_dep"]], compare(opal_tr, truth)[["max_dep"]]),
  pct_ss3 = c(NA, NA, compare(opal_tr, ss3)[["mean_pct"]]),
  dep_ss3 = c(NA, NA, compare(opal_tr, ss3)[["max_dep"]]))
knitr::kable(tab, digits = c(0, 2, 2, 3, 1, 3, 1, 3), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Model", "B0 (million t)", "B0 / true B0", "Terminal SSB / B0",
                           "SSB mean |% diff| from truth", "Max |depletion diff| from truth",
                           "SSB mean |% diff| from SS3", "Max |depletion diff| from SS3"))
```

```{r}
#| label: recruitment
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Recruitment deviations, opal AGE-SF against SS3. opal's deviation for time step t sets the age-1 recruits entering at t + 1. The truth's recruitment is not part of the bundled reference values."
rd <- merge(data.frame(ts = seq_along(opal_m$rdev), opal = opal_m$rdev),
            ref$ss3$recdevs, by = "ts")
ggplot(rd, aes(recdev, opal)) +
  geom_abline(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6, colour = series_col[["opal AGE-SF"]]) +
  labs(x = "SS3 recruitment deviation", y = "opal recruitment deviation")
```

# Fits to the data

The truth has no fits to the data, and its selectivity is defined by gear
and cell, so this section compares SS3 and opal only.

## Index

```{r}
#| label: index-fits
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Observed longline index (points, ±1.96 SE) with SS3's expected values and opal's predictions. Each quarterly series is on a mean-one scale."
cp <- d$cpue_data
idx <- data.frame(ts = cp$ts, fishery = cp$fishery, obs = cp$value, se = cp$se,
                  pred = opal_m$cpue$pred)
pred <- rbind(data.frame(ts = ref$ss3$cpue$ts, fishery = ref$ss3$cpue$fishery,
                         value = ref$ss3$cpue$expected, series = "SS3"),
              data.frame(ts = idx$ts, fishery = idx$fishery, value = idx$pred,
                         series = "opal AGE-SF"))
pred$series <- factor(pred$series, names(series_col))
ggplot() +
  geom_linerange(data = idx, aes(ts, ymin = obs * exp(-1.96 * se), ymax = obs * exp(1.96 * se)),
                 colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(data = idx, aes(ts, obs), size = 1, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(data = pred, aes(ts, value, colour = series), linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ fishery, ncol = 1, labeller = as_labeller(fleet_name)) +
  scale_series +
  labs(x = "Time step (quarter)", y = "Index (mean = 1 per series)")
```

```{r}
#| label: index-rmse
rmse <- function(o, p) sqrt(mean((log(o) - log(p))^2))
knitr::kable(data.frame(model = c("SS3", "opal AGE-SF"),
                        rmse = c(rmse(ref$ss3$cpue$obs, ref$ss3$cpue$expected),
                                 rmse(idx$obs, idx$pred))),
             digits = 4, col.names = c("Model", "RMSE of log index residuals"))
```

## Length compositions

```{r}
#| label: comp-aggregate
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Length compositions aggregated over all observations for each fishery, weighted by sample size: observed (bars), SS3's expected values and opal's predictions."
agg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(d$lf_fishery_f), function(j) {
  obs <- d$lf_obs_data$obs[[j]]
  obs <- obs / rowSums(obs)
  n   <- d$lf_n_fi[[j]]
  data.frame(fishery = d$lf_fishery_f[j], bin = d$len_lower,
             observed = colSums(obs * n) / sum(n))
}))
lines <- rbind(
  data.frame(fishery = ref$ss3$lf$fishery, bin = ref$ss3$lf$bin,
             value = ref$ss3$lf$expected, series = "SS3"),
  data.frame(fishery = opal_m$lf$fishery, bin = opal_m$lf$bin,
             value = opal_m$lf$predicted, series = "opal AGE-SF"))
lines$series <- factor(lines$series, names(series_col))
width <- diff(d$len_lower[1:2])
ggplot() +
  geom_col(data = agg, aes(bin + width / 2, observed), fill = "grey80", width = width) +
  geom_line(data = lines, aes(bin + width / 2, value, colour = series), linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ fishery, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y", labeller = as_labeller(fleet_name)) +
  scale_series +
  labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Proportion")
```

## Index size compositions

```{r}
#| label: sizefreq-fit
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "Index size compositions aggregated over all observations, weighted by sample size: observed (bars), SS3's expected values and opal's predictions."
agg_sf <- function(p, v) {
  a <- tapply(p[[v]] * p$nsamp, p$bin, sum)
  data.frame(bin = as.numeric(names(a)), value = as.numeric(a / sum(a)))
}
p_sf <- sf_pred("age_sf")
lines_sf <- rbind(data.frame(agg_sf(p_sf, "expected"), series = "SS3"),
                  data.frame(agg_sf(p_sf, "predicted"), series = "opal AGE-SF"))
lines_sf$series <- factor(lines_sf$series, names(series_col))
ggplot() +
  geom_col(data = agg_sf(p_sf, "obs"), aes(bin + 5, value), fill = "grey80", width = 10) +
  geom_line(data = lines_sf, aes(bin + 5, value, colour = series), linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_series +
  labs(x = "Length (cm; the last bin is 160 cm and above)", y = "Proportion")
```

```{r}
#| label: sizefreq-like
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  model = c("SS3", "opal AGE-SF"),
  like = c(ss3_like(p_sf$obs, p_sf$expected, p_sf$nsamp),
           ss3_like(p_sf$obs, p_sf$predicted, p_sf$nsamp))),
  digits = 1, col.names = c("Model", "SS3-style likelihood of the index size compositions"))
```

## Selectivity

```{r}
#| label: sel-age
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Selectivity-at-age: SS3 and opal AGE-SF."
sa <- rbind(data.frame(ref$ss3$sel_age, series = "SS3"),
            data.frame(opal_m$sel_age, series = "opal AGE-SF"))
sa$series <- factor(sa$series, names(series_col))
ggplot(sa[sa$fishery <= 17, ], aes(age, sel, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ fishery, ncol = 4, labeller = as_labeller(fleet_name)) +
  scale_series +
  labs(x = "Age (quarters)", y = "Selectivity")
```

```{r}
#| label: a50
a50 <- function(sa) {
  s <- sa[sa$fishery == 17, ]
  stats::approx(s$sel, s$age, 0.5, ties = "ordered")$y
}
a50_ss3 <- a50(ref$ss3$sel_age)
a50_opal <- a50(opal_m$sel_age)
```

Fisheries 15 and 16 mirror 14, and panel 17 stands for all four quarterly
index series. The index reaches 50% selectivity at
`r fmt(a50_opal, 1)` quarters in opal and `r fmt(a50_ss3, 1)` in SS3; SS3's
estimate sits at its lower bound of 8 quarters, which opal does not impose.

# Summary

```{r}
#| label: summary-values
dep_t <- last(truth, "static_dep")
dep_s <- last(ss3, "static_dep")
dep_o <- last(opal_tr, "static_dep")
```

* **Against the truth.** Neither single-region assessment is the truth. The
  operating model has movement among 159 cells and spatially varying
  recruitment, which neither represents. SS3's B0 is
  `r fmt(ref$ss3$ssb0 / ref$truth$b0, 2)` × the true B0 and opal AGE-SF's
  `r fmt(opal_m$B0 / ref$truth$b0, 2)` ×; terminal depletion is
  `r fmt(dep_s, 3)` (SS3) and `r fmt(dep_o, 3)` (opal), against a true
  `r fmt(dep_t, 3)`.
* **Against SS3.** With SS3's growth, selectivity curves and mirrors, index
  size compositions and lambda, opal AGE-SF's B0 is
  `r fmt(opal_m$B0 / ref$ss3$ssb0, 2)` × SS3's, and its spawning biomass
  differs from SS3's by `r fmt(compare(opal_tr, ss3)[["mean_pct"]], 1)`% on
  average. The fit converges and passes `opal_check()`.
* **What remains.** The rest of the gap to SS3 lies in the structural
  differences that stay: catch removed at the start of the quarter rather
  than through it (up to 10% of spawning biomass at SS3's own parameters),
  four quarterly catchabilities rather than one, and unconstrained
  recruitment deviations. It also depends on which optimum each model is
  in. Removing opal's priors as well (AGE-SF-NP, SS3's configuration)
  changes the stock status little, but leaves some selectivity parameters
  unidentified.

# Credit and references

The simulated example and the SS3 estimation model both come from the
Spatial Stock Assessment Simulation Experiment. The SS3 model was developed
by the IATTC analyst team (Mark N. Maunder, Haikun Xu and Carolina
Minte-Vera, Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission) as their submission to
it. The experiment's design, its operating models and the evaluation of the
submitted assessments, including theirs, are described in:

* Goethel, D.R., et al. (2024). 'Drivin' with your eyes closed': Results from
  an international, blinded simulation experiment to evaluate spatial stock
  assessments. *Fish and Fisheries* 25(3): 471–490.
  <https://doi.org/10.1111/faf.12819>

The age-specific K growth model is Stock Synthesis' `GrowthModel 3`:

* Methot, R.D. Jr., and Wetzel, C.R. (2013). Stock synthesis: A biological
  and statistical framework for fish stock assessment and fishery
  management. *Fisheries Research* 142: 86–99.
  <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fishres.2012.10.012>

The data and the simulated truth are from replicate 4 of the Indian Ocean
yellowfin operating model
(<https://github.com/aaronmberger-nwfsc/Spatial-Assessment-Modeling-Workshop>).
The IOTC working-party papers below have no DOI, so they link to the IOTC
document archive where a copy is available:

* Dunn, A., Rasmussen, S. and Mormede, S. (2015). Spatial Population Model.
  NIWA Technical Report 138.
* Dunn, A., Hoyle, S. and Datta, S. (2020). Development of spatially
  explicit operating models for yellowfin tuna populations in the Indian
  Ocean. IOTC-2020-WPTT22(AS)-19_Rev1.
  <https://iotc.org/sites/default/files/documents/2020/10/IOTC-2020-WPTT22AS-19_Rev1.pdf>
* Fu, D., Langley, A., Merino, G. and Urtizberea, A. (2018). Preliminary
  Indian Ocean yellowfin tuna stock assessment 1950–2017 (Stock Synthesis).
  IOTC-2018-WPTT20-33.
  <https://iotc.org/sites/default/files/documents/2018/10/IOTC-2018-WPTT20-33.pdf>
* Fonteneau, A. and Gascuel, D. (2008). Growth rates and apparent growth
  curves, for yellowfin, skipjack and bigeye tagged and recovered in the
  Indian Ocean during the IOTTP. IOTC-2008-WPTDA-08.

The SS3-to-opal converter is in <`r ref$source$repository`> (`code/rtmb`);
the bundled data were exported by `r ref$source$script` at commit
`r ref$source$commit`, and SS3's size compositions and lambdas by
`r ref$source$sizefreq_script`. The opal outputs shown were computed with
opal `r cache$opal` (commit `r cache$commit`) by
`data-raw/generate-io-yft-fits.R` and
`data-raw/generate-io-yft-vignette-cache.R`.
